title: ChatGPT names an insulinoma that three years of specialist visits had missed; a Madrid internist confirms it and surgery cures the 35-year-old
summary: ChatGPT suggested an insulinoma after three undiagnosed years; a glucose sensor and ER blood tests confirmed it and surgery cured him.
account: Dani, 35, had three years of tingling, numbness, dizziness, double vision and a 15 kg weight gain. A neurologist and a primary-care doctor called them nothing important. He entered his symptoms, results and history into ChatGPT, which named an insulinoma as the likely cause. He bought a glucose sensor and recorded readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL. He went to an emergency department. An internist at Hospital Puerta de Hierro Majadahonda, Madrid, confirmed an insulinoma by blood tests. A month and a half later surgeons removed about two thirds of his pancreas and his symptoms went. His video was posted on Instagram on 3 August 2025. The dates of the query, visit and surgery were not given.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant. Dani used it as a diagnostic aid, entering symptoms, results and history. OpenAI told the Mirror that its services “are not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition”. The Economic Times quoted that. So this benefit lay outside the product's stated purpose.
model_version: Not named; Dani said he used 'el modelo más inteligente de ChatGPT' (the most intelligent ChatGPT model)
segment: Consumer use of a general chatbot as a diagnostic aid

ratings.reason: A tumor that had gone undiagnosed for three years, producing glucose readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL, was found and removed. Dani says he is cured. He and the outlets call it life-saving (El Español: episodes that could have ended in fainting, brain damage or death). But that counterfactual and the whole chain rest on his own account. No clinician has spoken.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT produced the insulinoma hypothesis from a history that two doctors had reviewed without reaching it. That prompted the glucose sensor and the emergency visit. The diagnosis was made by an internist who, Dani wrote, “lo identificó sin nosotros decirle lo que creíamos que era”. The surgery and recovery were the hospital's work. Dani says he is not a doctor but has “formación biosanitaria de muchos años”, which let him understand what he was doing. Every account traces to his own video.

produced_by: A rare condition (Dani: “una enfermedad muy poco común (1 entre 1millon)”) with diffuse symptoms. A neurologist, after neck and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, and a primary-care doctor had dismissed them over three years.
A user with “formación biosanitaria de muchos años” who entered the full symptom list, test results and clinical history into the chatbot. He could interpret its answer.
A cheap self-test, a continuous glucose sensor, that could corroborate the hypothesis before the emergency visit. It read 30 to 40 mg/dL at night and between meals.
An emergency internist at Puerta de Hierro who confirmed the insulinoma by blood tests, and a surgical team that removed two thirds of the pancreas.
must_hold: The chatbot's hypothesis is treated as a reason to be tested, not as a diagnosis. Dani says he went to doctors before, during and after.
The suspected condition has an objective marker that a patient or clinician can measure quickly.
The user can state symptoms and prior results in enough detail for the model to rank a rare cause. Two doctors had the same information.

echoes.setting: AIBD-0038: ChatGPT proposes ALMS1 for a 44-year-old nephrology patient (consumer chatbot supplies a rare diagnosis that clinicians then confirm).
AIBD-0060: ChatGPT suggests tethered cord syndrome for a child seen by 17 doctors.

headline: ChatGPT names an insulinoma doctors missed for three years
metric: surgeons removed about two thirds of his pancreas and his symptoms went

comparator.against: three years of visits to specialists, including a neurologist, and a primary-care doctor
comparator.before: Tras varias pruebas le “dijeron que no era nada”
comparator.after: en pocos minutos su diagnóstico señalaba como posible principal causa de lo que me sucedía: un tumor de páncreas, un insulinoma
comparator.quote: En ese momento de desesperación fue cuando decidió meter todos sus “síntomas, los resultados médicos, el historial clínico al modelo más inteligente de ChatGPT”, señaló. Y según él “en pocos minutos su diagnóstico señalaba como posible principal causa de lo que me sucedía: un tumor de páncreas, un insulinoma”.

later.note: The surgery and the disappearance of his symptoms were already in the 3 August 2025 video; no later report on Dani was found, only re-reports of the same story.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as specific harm prevented as the classifier proposed: the harm was specific (an undiagnosed insulinoma with glucose readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL) and the supporting evidence is the internist's confirmation and the surgery; the counterfactual that doctors would not have found it rests on three years without a diagnosis. The Monitor also lists El Imparcial, which adds “enfermero” and a Reuters credit that the first-hand sources do not support, so it was not used. The Instagram reel was dated from its page metadata (3 August 2025); the video opens with “hoy me operan”, so the surgery predates the post, but no date was found. No hospital statement was found.
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Knowledge Discovery among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against from the cited sources.
Country of the developer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

claim_basis: Three independent news reports and the beneficiary's other are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
